signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags a sharp weekly divergence, with AUD leading the board at +1.134% across 4 pairs while CHF lags at −0.585% across 6 pairs. That generates a 1.719% leader-to-laggard spread, crossing the threshold for a strong thematic signal. A pre-computed cross rate differential of RBA 4.6% vs SNB 0.0% provides a 460bp carry advantage favoring AUD, further reinforced by OIS pricing where AONIA at 4.60% commands a 466bp premium over SARON at −0.06%. Spot AUD/CHF trades at 0.5840, extending its run as normal volatility keeps high-carry expressions supported against low-yielding funding currencies. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF, underpinned by the 460bp nominal policy spread and wide G10 performance gap. Catalyst: RBA meeting 3 Nov — hike bias priced. Risk: Broad equity risk-off forces rapid carry compression, accelerating flows back into CHF.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry Tension
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.84, holding above its SMA20 at 157.91 and SMA50 at 157.47 within a tight range-bound box below the SMA200 at 158.53. The Fed 4.0% vs BoJ 1.25% policy differential provides a 275bp carry advantage favoring USD, while OIS SOFR 3.93% vs TONA 1.23% confirms a 270bp spread. In the options market, 1M 25d risk reversals show a pronounced put skew of −2.18, signaling persistent downside hedging demand despite CFTC JPY leveraged funds holding net short −25,598 contracts. Furthermore, 160.00 remains the key psychological barrier that has previously triggered intervention concerns, keeping upside momentum constrained ahead of imminent event risk. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY, balancing the 270bp OIS carry advantage against strong options downside hedging. Catalyst: BoJ Interest Rate Decision ~02:30 UTC — hold expected. Risk: BoJ delivers an unexpected hawkish hike, triggering an aggressive unwind of net short JPY speculative positioning.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1157, continuing its established downtrend below its falling SMA20 at 1.1218, SMA50 at 1.1423, and SMA200 at 1.1572. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds net short −94,138 contracts, sitting at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of −1.72, confirming extreme institutional crowding on the short side. At the same time, 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 6.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.1%, producing an elevated vol risk premium of +2.4 points. Meanwhile, Fed 4.0% vs ECB 2.65% maintains a 135bp rate spread favoring USD, while SOFR vs €STR shows a 149bp carry advantage. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, supported by structural rate differentials while acknowledging short-squeeze vulnerability from crowded positioning. Catalyst: ECB Interest Rate Decision 29 Oct at 13:15 UTC — hold expected. Risk: Hawkish forward guidance from the ECB sparks rapid covering across the stretched spec short base.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Technical Downtrend + Retail Extreme
signals.text: USD/NOK prints at 9.334, maintaining an unbroken downtrend below its falling SMA20 at 9.479, SMA50 at 9.408, and SMA200 at 9.507. Retail positioning from Retail sentiment data shows a 100% long reading, placing retail market participants entirely against the prevailing technical trend structure. Simultaneously, sovereign rate momentum shows the 2-year yield spread between Norway and the US expanding +15bp over the last 20 sessions to +3bp, providing marginal yield support to the krone. With Brent and WTI crude trading higher at $102.0/bbl following Middle East transit developments, energy terms-of-trade continue to underpin NOK. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, trend-following with contrarian support against one-sided retail exposure. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy meeting 5 Nov — hold expected. Risk: A sharp pullback in crude oil prices below key support re-establishes upward momentum in the pair.
